summary: Kosmos Lookout, Lewis County, WA: WWII-surplus steel tower built 1947, replaced by a wooden tower in 1963, destroyed 1968; footings remain on Champion Timber land.

facts.design: World War II surplus steel observation tower with 7-by-7-foot cab and a house for living quarters (1947); replaced in 1963 by a 50-foot wooden DNR live-in tower
facts.status_note: Wooden tower destroyed in 1968 (register says removed). Sources describe only footings and house foundations on site
facts.agency: Washington State Division of Forestry/DNR built and ran the tower; the register lists Champion Timber as administrator and the site's owner today

staffing.status: manned by Mrs. V. Bridges in 1955; no later staffing found in sources read

access.note: Site owned by Champion Timber. Willhite reports a gate on the access road, signed open for non-motorized use in 2015 and changing during logging

visit.trail_note: No tower remains. Willhite describes a road east from Morton on Highway 12 with a gate partway up

events.note: World War II surplus steel tower with 7x7 cab and 14x18 house; reported as 75 ft in the annual report and as 90 ft (or 75) by Willhite
Newspaper reports the state added the Kosmos lookout, manned by Mrs. V. Bridges, who reported planes to the filter center
50-foot wooden DNR live-in tower replaced the steel tower on the same spot. A state report for 1960-62 also lists a Kosmos lookout among nine completed; see resolved_conflicts
Fire Lookout website and Willhite say destroyed; the register says abruptly removed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register September 28, 2010

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1947 annual report (quoted on the weebly page) gives 75 feet; Willhite gives 90 feet or 75 feet. The story reports both and does not choose one.
The register, the Fire Lookout website and Willhite date the 50-foot wooden tower to 1963, but a state report for 1960-62 lists a Kosmos lookout among nine completed in those years.
The register says it was abruptly removed in 1968; the Fire Lookout website and Willhite say destroyed. All agree it was gone after 1968.

The register lists Champion Timber as administrator and owner; the Fire Lookout website and the 1947 annual report credit the Washington Division of Forestry/DNR with building and running the tower. The story separates the builder from the current owner.

notes_for_editor: Build, replacement and fate are agreed across four sources; height (75 vs 90 ft) and the 1963 vs 1960-62 date are unresolved and reported as such. The brief's agency 'Champion Timber' is the register's administrator line; the state built the tower, so the record separates the two. Access is inferred from company ownership and a gate, not from a published rule. The Fire Lookout website credits Washington Digital Archives and Fire Lookout Museum photos that were not fetched, so there are no new photo entries. No staffing after 1955 was found.
